You can use the `Content` component to add content that is specific to the Pages Router. Any shared content should not be wrapped in a component. */} 8 9 ## Upgrading from 15 to 16 10 11 ### Using AI Agents with Next.js DevTools MCP 12 13 If you're using an AI coding assistant that supports the [Model Context Protocol (MCP)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io), you can use the **Next.js DevTools MCP** to automate the upgrade process and migration tasks. 14 15 #### Setup 16 17 Add the following configuration to your MCP client, for each coding agent you can read [this section](https://github.com/vercel/next-devtools-mcp#mcp-client-configuration) for configuration details. 18 19 **example:** 20 21 ```json filename=".mcp.json" 22 { 23 "mcpServers": { 24 "next-devtools": { 25 "command": "npx", 26 "args": ["-y", "next-devtools-mcp@latest"] 27 } 28 } 29 } 30 ``` 31 32 For more information, visit the [`next-devtools-mcp`](https://github.com/vercel/next-devtools-mcp) documentation to configure with your MCP client. 33 34 > **Note:** Using `next-devtools-mcp@latest` ensures that your MCP client will always use the latest version of the Next.js DevTools MCP server. 35 36 #### Example Prompts 37 38 Once configured, you can use natural language prompts to upgrade your Next.js app: 39 40 **To upgrade to Next.js 16:** 41 42 Connect to your coding agent and then prompt: 43 44 ```txt 45 Next Devtools, help me upgrade my Next.js app to version 16 46 ``` 47 48 **To migrate to Cache Components (after upgrading to v16):** 49 50 Connect to your coding agent and then prompt: 51 52 ```txt 53 Next Devtools, migrate my Next.js app to cache components 54 ``` 55 56 Learn more in the documentation [here](/docs/app/guides/mcp). 57 58 ### Using the Codemod 59 60 To update to Next.js version 16, you can use the `upgrade` [codemod](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#160): 61 62 ```bash package="pnpm" 63 pnpm dlx @next/codemod@canary upgrade latest 64 ``` 65 66 ```bash package="npm" 67 npx @next/codemod@canary upgrade latest 68 ``` 69 70 ```bash package="yarn" 71 yarn dlx @next/codemod@canary upgrade latest 72 ``` 73 74 ```bash package="bun" 75 bunx @next/codemod@canary upgrade latest 76 ``` 77 78 The [codemod](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#160) is able to: 79 80 - Update `next.config.js` to use the new `turbopack` configuration 81 - Migrate from `next lint` to the ESLint CLI 82 - Migrate from deprecated `middleware` convention to `proxy` 83 - Remove `unstable_` prefix from stabilized APIs 84 - Remove `experimental_ppr` Route Segment Config from pages and layouts 85 86 If you prefer to do it manually, install the latest Next.js and React versions: 87 88 ```bash package="pnpm" 89 pnpm add next@latest react@latest react-dom@latest 90 ``` 91 92 ```bash package="npm" 93 npm install next@latest react@latest react-dom@latest 94 ``` 95 96 ```bash package="yarn" 97 yarn add next@latest react@latest react-dom@latest 98 ``` 99 100 ```bash package="bun" 101 bun add next@latest react@latest react-dom@latest 102 ``` 103 104 If you are using TypeScript, ensure you also upgrade `@types/react` and `@types/react-dom` to their latest versions. 105 106 ## Node.js runtime and browser support 107 108 | Requirement | Change / Details | 109 | ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | 110 | Node.js 20.9+ | Minimum version now `20.9.0` (LTS); Node.js 18 no longer supported | 111 | TypeScript 5+ | Minimum version now `5.1.0` | 112 | Browsers | Chrome 111+, Edge 111+, Firefox 111+, Safari 16.4+ | 113 114 ## Turbopack by default 115 116 Starting with **Next.js 16**, Turbopack is stable and used by default with `next dev` and `next build` 117 118 Previously you had to enable Turbopack using `--turbopack`, or `--turbo`. 119 120 ```json filename="package.json" 121 { 122 "scripts": { 123 "dev": "next dev --turbopack", 124 "build": "next build --turbopack", 125 "start": "next start" 126 } 127 } 128 ``` 129 130 This is no longer necessary. You can update your `package.json` scripts: 131 132 ```json filename="package.json" 133 { 134 "scripts": { 135 "dev": "next dev", 136 "build": "next build", 137 "start": "next start" 138 } 139 } 140 ``` 141 142 If your project has a [custom `webpack`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/webpack) configuration and you run `next build` (which now uses Turbopack by default), the build will **fail** to prevent misconfiguration issues. 143 144 You have a few different ways to address this: 145 146 - **Use Turbopack anyway:** Run with `next build --turbopack` to build using Turbopack and ignore your `webpack` config. 147 - **Switch to Turbopack fully:** Migrate your `webpack` config to Turbopack-compatible options. 148 - **Keep using Webpack:** Use the `--webpack` flag to opt out of Turbopack and build with Webpack. 149 150 > **Good to know**: If you see failing builds because a `webpack` configuration was found, but you don't define one yourself, it is likely that a plugin is adding a `webpack` option 151 152 ### Opting out of Turbopack 153 154 If you need to continue using Webpack, you can opt out with the `--webpack` flag. For example, to use Turbopack in development but Webpack for production builds: 155 156 ```json filename="package.json" 157 { 158 "scripts": { 159 "dev": "next dev", 160 "build": "next build --webpack", 161 "start": "next start" 162 } 163 } 164 ``` 165 166 We recommend using Turbopack for development and production. Submit a comment to this [thread](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions/77721), if you are unable to switch to Turbopack. 167 168 ### Turbopack configuration location 169 170 The `experimental.turbopack` configuration is out of experimental. 171 172 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" 173 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 174 175 // Next.js 15 - experimental.turbopack 176 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 177 experimental: { 178 turbopack: { 179 // options 180 }, 181 }, 182 } 183 184 export default nextConfig 185 ``` 186 187 You can use it as a top-level `turbopack` option: 188 189 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" 190 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 191 192 // Next.js 16 - turbopack at the top level of nextConfig 193 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 194 turbopack: { 195 // options 196 }, 197 } 198 199 export default nextConfig 200 ``` 201 202 Make sure to review the `Turbopack` configuration [options](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/turbopack). **Next.js 16** introduces various improvements and new options, for example: 203 204 - [Advanced Webpack loader conditions](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/turbopack#advanced-webpack-loader-conditions) 205 - [debugIds](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/turbopack#debug-ids) 206 207 ### Resolve alias fallback 208 209 In some projects, client-side code may import files containing Node.js native modules. This will cause `Module not found: Can't resolve 'fs'` type of errors. 210 211 When this happens, you should refactor your code so that your client-side bundles do not reference these Node.js native modules. 212 213 However, in some cases, this might not be possible. In Webpack the `resolve.fallback` option was typically used to **silence** the error. Turbopack offers a similar option, using `turbopack.resolveAlias`. In this case, tell Turbopack to load an empty module when `fs` is requested for the browser. 214 215 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" 216 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 217 218 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 219 turbopack: { 220 resolveAlias: { 221 fs: { 222 browser: './empty.ts', // We recommend to fix code imports before using this method 223 }, 224 }, 225 }, 226 } 227 228 export default nextConfig 229 ``` 230 231 It is preferable to refactor your modules so that client code doesn't ever import from modules using Node.js native modules. 232 233 ### Sass node_modules imports 234 235 Turbopack fully supports importing Sass files from `node_modules`. Note that while Webpack allowed the legacy tilde (`~`) prefix, Turbopack does not support this syntax. 236 237 In Webpack: 238 239 ```scss filename="styles/globals.scss" 240 @import '~bootstrap/dist/css/bootstrap.min.css'; 241 ``` 242 243 In Turbopack: 244 245 ```scss filename="styles/globals.scss" 246 @import 'bootstrap/dist/css/bootstrap.min.css'; 247 ``` 248 249 If changing the imports is not possible, you can use `turbopack.resolveAlias`. For example: 250 251 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" 252 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 253 254 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 255 turbopack: { 256 resolveAlias: { 257 '~*': '*', 258 }, 259 }, 260 } 261 262 export default nextConfig 263 ``` 264 265 ### Turbopack File System Caching (beta) 266 267 Turbopack now supports filesystem caching in development, storing compiler artifacts on disk between runs for significantly faster compile times across restarts. 268 269 Enable filesystem caching in your configuration: 270 271 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 272 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 273 274 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 275 experimental: { 276 turbopackFileSystemCacheForDev: true, 277 }, 278 } 279 280 export default nextConfig 281 ``` 282 283 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 284 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 285 const nextConfig = { 286 experimental: { 287 turbopackFileSystemCacheForDev: true, 288 }, 289 } 290 291 module.exports = nextConfig 292 ``` 293 294 ## Async Request APIs (Breaking change) 295 296 Version 15 introduced [Async Request APIs](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-15#async-request-apis-breaking-change) as a breaking change, with **temporary** synchronous compatibility. 297 298 Starting with **Next.js 16**, synchronous access is fully removed. These APIs can only be accessed asynchronously. 299 300 - [`cookies`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cookies) 301 - [`headers`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/headers) 302 - [`draftMode`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/draft-mode) 303 - `params` in [`layout.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout), [`page.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page), [`route.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route), [`default.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/default), [`opengraph-image`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/metadata/opengraph-image#opengraph-image), [`twitter-image`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/metadata/opengraph-image#twitter-image), [`icon`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/metadata/app-icons#icon), and [`apple-icon`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/metadata/app-icons#apple-icon). 304 - `searchParams` in [`page.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page) 305 306 Use the [codemod](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#migrate-to-async-dynamic-apis) to migrate to async Request-time APIs. 307 308 ### Migrating types for async Request-time APIs 309 310 To help migrate to async `params` and `searchParams`, you can run [`npx next typegen`](/docs/app/api-reference/cli/next#next-typegen-options) to automatically generate these globally available types helpers: 311 312 - [`PageProps`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#page-props-helper) 313 - [`LayoutProps`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout#layout-props-helper) 314 - [`RouteContext`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route#route-context-helper) 315 316 > **Good to know**: `typegen` was introduced in Next.js 15.5 317 318 This simplifies type-safe migration to the new async API pattern, and enables you to update your components with full type safety, for example: 319 320 ```tsx filename="/app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx" 321 export default async function Page(props: PageProps<'/blog/[slug]'>) { 322 const { slug } = await props.params 323 const query = await props.searchParams 324 return

Blog Post: {slug}

325 } 326 ``` 327 328 This approach gives you fully type-safe access to `props.params`, including the `slug`, and to `searchParams`, directly within your page. 329 330 ## Async parameters for icon, and open-graph Image (Breaking change) 331 332 > The props passed to the image generating functions in `opengraph-image`, `twitter-image`, `icon`, and `apple-icon`, are now Promises. 333 334 In previous versions, both the `Image` (image generation function), and the `generateImageMetadata` received a `params` object. The `id` returned by `generateImageMetadata` was passed as a string to the image generation function. 335 336 ```js filename="app/shop/[slug]/opengraph-image.js" 337 // Next.js 15 - synchronous params access 338 export function generateImageMetadata({ params }) { 339 const { slug } = params 340 return [{ id: '1' }, { id: '2' }] 341 } 342 343 // Next.js 15 - synchronous params and id access 344 export default function Image({ params, id }) { 345 const slug = params.slug 346 const imageId = id // string 347 // ... 348 } 349 ``` 350 351 Starting with **Next.js 16**, to align with the [Async Request APIs](#async-request-apis-breaking-change) change, the image generating function now receives `params` and `id` as promises. The `generateImageMetadata` function continues to receive synchronous `params`. 352 353 ```js filename="app/shop/[slug]/opengraph-image.js" 354 export async function generateImageMetadata({ params }) { 355 const { slug } = params 356 return [{ id: '1' }, { id: '2' }] 357 } 358 359 // Next.js 16 - asynchronous params and id access 360 export default async function Image({ params, id }) { 361 const { slug } = await params // params now async 362 const imageId = await id // id is now Promise when using generateImageMetadata 363 // ... 364 } 365 ``` 366 367 ## Async `id` parameter for `sitemap` (Breaking change) 368 369 Previously, the `id` values returned from [`generateSitemaps`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-sitemaps) were passed directly to the `sitemap` generating function. 370 371 ```js filename="app/product/sitemap.js" 372 export async function generateSitemaps() { 373 return [{ id: 0 }, { id: 1 }, { id: 2 }, { id: 3 }] 374 } 375 376 // Next.js 15 - synchronous id access 377 export default async function sitemap({ id }) { 378 const start = id * 50000 // id is a number 379 // ... 380 } 381 ``` 382 383 Starting with **Next.js 16**, the `sitemap` generating function now receives `id` as a promise. 384 385 ```js filename="app/product/sitemap.js" 386 export async function generateSitemaps() { 387 return [{ id: 0 }, { id: 1 }, { id: 2 }, { id: 3 }] 388 } 389 390 // Next.js 16 - asynchronous id access 391 export default async function sitemap({ id }) { 392 const resolvedId = await id // id is now Promise 393 const start = Number(resolvedId) * 50000 394 // ... 395 } 396 ``` 397 398 ## React 19.2 399 400 The App Router in **Next.js 16** uses the latest React [Canary release](https://react.dev/blog/2023/05/03/react-canaries), which includes the newly released React 19.2 features and other features being incrementally stabilized. Highlights include: 401 402 - **[View Transitions](https://react.dev/reference/react/ViewTransition)**: Animate elements that update inside a Transition or navigation 403 - **[`useEffectEvent`](https://react.dev/reference/react/useEffectEvent)**: Extract non-reactive logic from Effects into reusable Effect Event functions 404 - **[Activity](https://react.dev/reference/react/Activity)**: Render "background activity" by hiding UI with `display: none` while maintaining state and cleaning up Effects 405 406 Learn more in the [React 19.2 announcement](https://react.dev/blog/2025/10/01/react-19-2). 407 408 ## React Compiler Support 409 410 Built-in support for the React Compiler is now stable in **Next.js 16** following the React Compiler's 1.0 release. The React Compiler automatically memoizes components, reducing unnecessary re-renders with zero manual code changes. 411 412 The `reactCompiler` configuration option has been promoted from `experimental` to stable. It is not enabled by default as we continue gathering build performance data across different application types. 413 414 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 415 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 416 417 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 418 reactCompiler: true, 419 } 420 421 export default nextConfig 422 ``` 423 424 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 425 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 426 const nextConfig = { 427 reactCompiler: true, 428 } 429 430 module.exports = nextConfig 431 ``` 432 433 Install the latest version of the React Compiler plugin: 434 435 ```bash package="pnpm" 436 pnpm add -D babel-plugin-react-compiler 437 ``` 438 439 ```bash package="npm" 440 npm install -D babel-plugin-react-compiler 441 ``` 442 443 ```bash package="yarn" 444 yarn add -D babel-plugin-react-compiler 445 ``` 446 447 ```bash package="bun" 448 bun add -D babel-plugin-react-compiler 449 ``` 450 451 > **Good to know:** Expect compile times in development and during builds to be higher when enabling this option as the React Compiler relies on Babel. 452 453 ## Caching APIs 454 455 ### revalidateTag 456 457 [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag) now requires a second argument specifying a [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife#reference) profile. Users receive stale content while fresh data loads in the background. 492 493 ### updateTag 494 495 [`updateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag) is a new [Server Actions](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data#what-are-server-functions)-only API that provides **read-your-writes** semantics, where a user makes a change and the UI immediately shows the change, rather than stale data. 496 497 It does this by expiring and immediately refreshing data within the same request. 498 499 ```ts filename="app/actions.ts" switcher 500 'use server' 501 502 import { updateTag } from 'next/cache' 503 504 export async function updateUserProfile(userId: string, profile: Profile) { 505 await db.users.update(userId, profile) 506 507 // Expire cache and refresh immediately - user sees their changes right away 508 updateTag(`user-${userId}`) 509 } 510 ``` 511 512 ```js filename="app/actions.js" switcher 513 'use server' 514 515 import { updateTag } from 'next/cache' 516 517 export async function updateUserProfile(userId, profile) { 518 await db.users.update(userId, profile) 519 520 // Expire cache and refresh immediately - user sees their changes right away 521 updateTag(`user-${userId}`) 522 } 523 ``` 524 525 This ensures interactive features reflect changes immediately. The `unstable_` prefix is no longer needed. 566 567 Wherever you had aliased imports like: 568 569 ```ts 570 import { 571 unstable_cacheLife as cacheLife, 572 unstable_cacheTag as cacheTag, 573 } from 'next/cache' 574 ``` 575 576 You can update your imports to: 577 578 ```ts 579 import { cacheLife, cacheTag } from 'next/cache' 580 ``` 581 582 ## Enhanced Routing and Navigation 583 584 **Next.js 16** includes a complete overhaul of the routing and navigation system, making page transitions leaner and faster. This optimizes how Next.js prefetches and caches navigation data: 585 586 - **Layout deduplication**: When prefetching multiple URLs with a shared layout, the layout is downloaded once. 587 - **Incremental prefetching**: Next.js only prefetches parts not already in cache, rather than entire pages. 588 589 These changes require **no code modifications** and are designed to improve performance across all apps. 590 591 However, you may see more individual prefetch requests with much lower total transfer sizes. We believe this is the right trade-off for nearly all applications. 592 593 If the increased request count causes issues, please let us know by creating an [issue](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/issues) or [discussion](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions) item. 594 595 ## Partial Prerendering (PPR) 596 597 **Next.js 16** removes the experimental **Partial Prerendering (PPR)** flag and configuration options, including the route level segment `experimental_ppr`. 598 599 Starting with **Next.js 16**, you can opt into PPR using the [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) configuration. 600 601 ```js filename="next.config.js" 602 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 603 const nextConfig = { 604 cacheComponents: true, 605 } 606 607 module.exports = nextConfig 608 ``` 609 610 PPR in **Next.js 16** works differently than in **Next.js 15** canaries. If you are using PPR today, stay in the current Next.js 15 canary you are using. See [Migrating to Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/migrating-to-cache-components) for migration patterns. 611 612 ```js filename="next.config.js" 613 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 614 const nextConfig = { 615 // If you are using PPR today 616 // stay in the current Next.js 15 canary 617 experimental: { 618 ppr: true, 619 }, 620 } 621 622 module.exports = nextConfig 623 ``` 624 625 ## `middleware` to `proxy` 626 627 The `middleware` filename is deprecated, and has been renamed to `proxy` to clarify network boundary and routing focus. 628 629 The `edge` runtime is **NOT** supported in `proxy`. The `proxy` runtime is `nodejs`, and it cannot be configured. If you want to continue using the `edge` runtime, keep using `middleware`. We will follow up on a minor release with further `edge` runtime instructions. 630 631 ```bash filename="Terminal" 632 # Rename your middleware file 633 mv middleware.ts proxy.ts 634 # or 635 mv middleware.js proxy.js 636 ``` 637 638 The named export `middleware` is also deprecated. Rename your function to `proxy`. 639 640 ```ts filename="proxy.ts" switcher 641 export function proxy(request: Request) {} 642 ``` 643 644 ```js filename="proxy.js" switcher 645 export function proxy(request) {} 646 ``` 647 648 We recommend changing the function name to `proxy`, even if you are using a default export. 649 650 Configuration flags that contained the `middleware` name are also renamed. For example, `skipMiddlewareUrlNormalize` is now `skipProxyUrlNormalize` 651 652 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 653 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 654 655 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 656 skipProxyUrlNormalize: true, 657 } 658 659 export default nextConfig 660 ``` 661 662 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 663 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 664 const nextConfig = { 665 skipProxyUrlNormalize: true, 666 } 667 668 module.exports = nextConfig 669 ``` 670 671 The version 16 [codemod](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#160) is able to update these flags too. 672 673 ## `next/image` changes 674 675 ### Local Images with Query Strings (Breaking change) 676 677 Local image sources with query strings now require `images.localPatterns.search` configuration to prevent enumeration attacks. 678 679 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" 680 import Image from 'next/image' 681 682 export default function Page() { 683 return 684 } 685 ``` 686 687 If you need to use query strings with local images, add the pattern to your configuration: 688 689 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 690 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 691 692 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 693 images: { 694 localPatterns: [ 695 { 696 pathname: '/assets/**', 697 search: '?v=1', 698 }, 699 ], 700 }, 701 } 702 703 export default nextConfig 704 ``` 705 706 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 707 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 708 const nextConfig = { 709 images: { 710 localPatterns: [ 711 { 712 pathname: '/assets/**', 713 search: '?v=1', 714 }, 715 ], 716 }, 717 } 718 719 module.exports = nextConfig 720 ``` 721 722 ### `minimumCacheTTL` Default (Breaking change) 723 724 The default value for `images.minimumCacheTTL` has changed from `60 seconds` to `4 hours` (14400 seconds). This reduces revalidation cost for images without cache-control headers. 725 726 For some Next.js users, image revalidation was happening frequently, often because the upstream source images missed a `cache-control` header. This caused revalidation to happen every `60` seconds, which increased CPU usage and cost. 727 728 Since most images do not change often, this short interval is not ideal. Setting the default to 4 hours offers a more durable cache by default, while still allowing images to update a few times per day if needed. 729 730 If you need the previous behavior, change `minimumCacheTTL` to a lower value, for example back to `60` seconds: 731 732 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 733 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 734 735 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 736 images: { 737 minimumCacheTTL: 60, 738 }, 739 } 740 741 export default nextConfig 742 ``` 743 744 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 745 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 746 const nextConfig = { 747 images: { 748 minimumCacheTTL: 60, 749 }, 750 } 751 752 module.exports = nextConfig 753 ``` 754 755 ### `imageSizes` Default (Breaking change) 756 757 The value `16` has been removed from the default `images.imageSizes` array. 758 759 We have looked at request analytics and found out that very few projects ever serve 16 pixels width images. Removing this setting reduces the size of the `srcset` attribute shipped to the browser by `next/image`. 760 761 If you need to support 16px images: 762 763 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 764 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 765 766 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 767 images: { 768 imageSizes: [16, 32, 48, 64, 96, 128, 256, 384], 769 }, 770 } 771 772 export default nextConfig 773 ``` 774 775 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 776 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 777 const nextConfig = { 778 images: { 779 imageSizes: [16, 32, 48, 64, 96, 128, 256, 384], 780 }, 781 } 782 783 module.exports = nextConfig 784 ``` 785 786 Rather than lack of developer usage, we believe 16 pixels width images have become less common, because `devicePixelRatio: 2` actually fetches a 32px image to prevent blurriness in retina displays. 787 788 ### `qualities` Default (Breaking change) 789 790 The default value for `images.qualities` has changed from allowing all qualities to only `[75]`. 791 792 If you need to support multiple quality levels: 793 794 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 795 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 796 797 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 798 images: { 799 qualities: [50, 75, 100], 800 }, 801 } 802 803 export default nextConfig 804 ``` 805 806 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 807 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 808 const nextConfig = { 809 images: { 810 qualities: [50, 75, 100], 811 }, 812 } 813 814 module.exports = nextConfig 815 ``` 816 817 If you specify a `quality` prop not included in the `image.qualities` array, the quality will be coerced to the closest value in `images.qualities`. For example, given the configuration above, a `quality` prop of 80, is coerced to 75. 818 819 ### Local IP Restriction (Breaking change) 820 821 A new security restriction blocks local IP optimization by default. Set `images.dangerouslyAllowLocalIP` to `true` only for private networks. 822 823 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 824 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 825 826 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 827 images: { 828 dangerouslyAllowLocalIP: true, // Only for private networks 829 }, 830 } 831 832 export default nextConfig 833 ``` 834 835 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 836 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 837 const nextConfig = { 838 images: { 839 dangerouslyAllowLocalIP: true, // Only for private networks 840 }, 841 } 842 843 module.exports = nextConfig 844 ``` 845 846 This might be necessary when hosting Next.js in a VPC with split-horizon DNS and you receive status 400 Bad Request. Only enable once you understand the SSRF risk. 847 848 ### Maximum Redirects (Breaking change) 849 850 The default for `images.maximumRedirects` has changed from unlimited to 3 redirects maximum. 851 852 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 853 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 854 855 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 856 images: { 857 maximumRedirects: 0, // Disable redirects 858 // or 859 maximumRedirects: 5, // Increase for edge cases 860 }, 861 } 862 863 export default nextConfig 864 ``` 865 866 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 867 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 868 const nextConfig = { 869 images: { 870 maximumRedirects: 0, // Disable redirects 871 // or 872 maximumRedirects: 5, // Increase for edge cases 873 }, 874 } 875 876 module.exports = nextConfig 877 ``` 878 879 ### `next/legacy/image` Component (deprecated) 880 881 The `next/legacy/image` component is deprecated. Use `next/image` instead: 882 883 ```tsx 884 // Before 885 import Image from 'next/legacy/image' 886 887 // After 888 import Image from 'next/image' 889 ``` 890 891 ### `images.domains` Configuration (deprecated) 892 893 The `images.domains` config is deprecated. 894 895 ```js filename="next.config.js" 896 // image.domains is deprecated 897 module.exports = { 898 images: { 899 domains: ['example.com'], 900 }, 901 } 902 ``` 903 904 Use `images.remotePatterns` instead for improved security: 905 906 ```js filename="next.config.js" 907 // Use image.remotePatterns instead 908 module.exports = { 909 images: { 910 remotePatterns: [ 911 { 912 protocol: 'https', 913 hostname: 'example.com', 914 }, 915 ], 916 }, 917 } 918 ``` 919 920 ## Concurrent `dev` and `build` 921 922 `next dev` and `next build` now use separate output directories, enabling concurrent execution. The `next dev` command outputs to `.next/dev`. 923 924 Additionally, a lockfile mechanism prevents multiple `next dev` or `next build` instances on the same project. 925 926 The [Turbopack tracing command](/docs/app/guides/local-development#turbopack-tracing) should be: 927 928 ```bash package="pnpm" 929 pnpm next internal trace .next-profiles/trace-turbopack 930 ``` 931 932 ```bash package="npm" 933 npx next internal trace .next-profiles/trace-turbopack 934 ``` 935 936 ```bash package="yarn" 937 yarn next internal trace .next-profiles/trace-turbopack 938 ``` 939 940 ```bash package="bun" 941 bunx next internal trace .next-profiles/trace-turbopack 942 ``` 943 944 ## Parallel Routes `default.js` requirement 945 946 All [parallel route](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/parallel-routes) slots now require explicit `default.js` files. Builds will fail without them. 947 948 To maintain previous behavior, create a [`default.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/default) file that calls `notFound()` or returns `null`. 949 950 ```tsx filename="app/@modal/default.tsx" 951 import { notFound } from 'next/navigation' 952 953 export default function Default() { 954 notFound() 955 } 956 ``` 957 958 Or return `null`: 959 960 ```tsx filename="app/@modal/default.tsx" 961 export default function Default() { 962 return null 963 } 964 ``` 965 966 ## ESLint Flat Config 967 968 `@next/eslint-plugin-next` now defaults to ESLint Flat Config format, aligning with ESLint v10 which will drop legacy config support. 969 970 Make sure to review our API reference for the [`@next/eslint-plugin-next`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/eslint#setup-eslint) plugin. 971 972 If you're using the legacy `.eslintrc` format, consider migrating to the flat config format. See the [ESLint migration guide](https://eslint.org/docs/latest/use/configure/migration-guide) for details. 973 974 ## Scroll Behavior Override 975 976 In **previous versions of Next.js**, if you had set `scroll-behavior: smooth` globally on your `` element via CSS, Next.js would override this during SPA route transitions, as follows: 977 978 1. Temporarily set `scroll-behavior` to `auto` 979 2. Perform the navigation (causing instant scroll to top) 980 3. Restore your original `scroll-behavior` value 981 982 This ensured that page navigation always felt snappy and instant, even when you had smooth scrolling enabled for in-page navigation. However, this manipulation could be expensive, especially at the start of every navigation. 983 984 In **Next.js 16**, this behavior has changed. By default, Next.js will **no longer override** your `scroll-behavior` setting during navigation. 985 986 **If you want Next.js to perform this override** (the previous default behavior), add the `data-scroll-behavior="smooth"` attribute to your `` element: 987 988 ```tsx filename="app/layout.tsx" 989 export default function RootLayout({ children }) { 990 return ( 991 992 {children} 993 994 ) 995 } 996 ``` 997 998 ## Performance Improvements 999 1000 Significant performance optimizations for `next dev` and `next start` commands, along with improved terminal output with clearer formatting, better error messages, and improved performance metrics. 1001 1002 **Next.js 16** removes the `size` and `First Load JS` metrics from the `next build` output. We found these to be inaccurate in server-driven architectures using React Server Components. Both our Turbopack and Webpack implementations had issues, and disagreed on how to account for Client Components payload. 1003 1004 The most effective way to measure actual route performance is through tools such as [Chrome Lighthouse](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/lighthouse/overview) or Vercel Analytics, which focus on Core Web Vitals and downloaded resource sizes. 1005 1006 ### `next dev` config load 1007 1008 In previous versions the Next config file was loaded twice during development: 1009 1010 - When running the `next dev` command 1011 - When the `next dev` command started the Next.js server 1012 1013 This was inefficient because the `next dev` command doesn't need the config file to start the Next.js server. 1014 1015 A consequence of this change is that, when running `next dev` checking if `process.argv` includes `'dev'`, in your Next.js config file, will return `false`. 1016 1017 > **Good to know**: The `typegen`, and `build` commands, are still visible in `process.argv`. 1018 1019 This is specially important for plugins that trigger side-effects on `next dev`. If that's the case, it might be enough to check if `NODE_ENV` is set to `development`. 1020 1021 ```js filename="next.config.js" 1022 import { startServer } from 'docs-lib/dev-server' 1023 1024 const isDev = process.env.NODE_ENV === 'development' 1025 1026 if (isDev) { 1027 startServer() 1028 } 1029 1030 const nextConfig = { 1031 /* Your config options */ 1032 } 1033 1034 module.exports = nextConfig 1035 ``` 1036 1037 Alternatively, use the [`phase`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js#phase) in which the configuration is loaded. 1038 1039 ## Build Adapters API (alpha) 1040 1041 Following the [Build Adapters RFC](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions/77740), the first alpha version of the Build Adapters API is now available. 1042 1043 Build Adapters allow you to create custom adapters that hook into the build process, enabling deployment platforms and custom build integrations to modify Next.js configuration or process build output. 1044 1045 ```js filename="next.config.js" 1046 const nextConfig = { 1047 experimental: { 1048 adapterPath: require.resolve('./my-adapter.js'), 1049 }, 1050 } 1051 1052 module.exports = nextConfig 1053 ``` 1054 1055 `adapterPath` was promoted to a stable, top-level option in 16.2.0. See [`adapterPath`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/adapterPath) for the current API reference. 1056 1057 ## Modern Sass API 1058 1059 `sass-loader` has been bumped to v16, which supports [modern Sass syntax](https://sass-lang.com/documentation/js-api/#md:usage) and new features. 1060 1061 ## Removals 1062 1063 These features were previously deprecated and are now removed: 1064 1065 ### AMP Support 1066 1067 AMP adoption has declined significantly, and maintaining this feature adds complexity to the framework. All AMP APIs and configurations have been removed: 1068 1069 - `amp` configuration from your Next config file 1070 - `next/amp` hook imports and usage (`useAmp`) 1071 1072 ```tsx 1073 // Removed 1074 import { useAmp } from 'next/amp' 1075 1076 // Removed 1077 export const config = { amp: true } 1078 ``` 1079 1080 - `export const config = { amp: true }` from pages 1081 1082 ```js filename="next.config.js" 1083 const nextConfig = { 1084 // Removed 1085 amp: { 1086 canonicalBase: 'https://example.com', 1087 }, 1088 } 1089 1090 export default nextConfig 1091 ``` 1092 1093 Evaluate if AMP is still necessary for your use case. Most performance benefits can now be achieved through Next.js's built-in optimizations and modern web standards. 1094 1095 ### `next lint` Command 1096 1097 The `next lint` command has been removed. Use Biome or ESLint directly. `next build` no longer runs linting. 1098 1099 A codemod is available to automate migration: 1100 1101 ```bash package="pnpm" 1102 pnpm dlx @next/codemod@canary next-lint-to-eslint-cli . 1103 ``` 1104 1105 ```bash package="npm" 1106 npx @next/codemod@canary next-lint-to-eslint-cli . 1107 ``` 1108 1109 ```bash package="yarn" 1110 yarn dlx @next/codemod@canary next-lint-to-eslint-cli . 1111 ``` 1112 1113 ```bash package="bun" 1114 bunx @next/codemod@canary next-lint-to-eslint-cli . 1115 ``` 1116 1117 The `eslint` option in the Next.js config file is also removed. 1118 1119 ```js filename="next.config.mjs" 1120 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 1121 const nextConfig = { 1122 // No longer supported 1123 // eslint: {}, 1124 } 1125 1126 export default nextConfig 1127 ``` 1128 1129 ### Runtime Configuration 1130 1131 `serverRuntimeConfig` and `publicRuntimeConfig` have been removed. Use environment variables instead. 1132 1133 **Before (Next.js 15):** 1134 1135 ```js filename="next.config.js" 1136 module.exports = { 1137 serverRuntimeConfig: { 1138 dbUrl: process.env.DATABASE_URL, 1139 }, 1140 publicRuntimeConfig: { 1141 apiUrl: '/api', 1142 }, 1143 } 1144 ``` 1145 1146 ```tsx filename="pages/index.tsx" 1147 import getConfig from 'next/config' 1148 1149 export default function Page() { 1150 const { publicRuntimeConfig } = getConfig() 1151 return

API URL: {publicRuntimeConfig.apiUrl}

1152 } 1153 ``` 1154 1155 **After (Next.js 16):** 1156 1157 For server-only values, access environment variables directly in Server Components: 1158 1159 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" 1160 async function fetchData() { 1161 const dbUrl = process.env.DATABASE_URL 1162 // Use for server-side operations only 1163 return await db.query(dbUrl, 'SELECT * FROM users') 1164 } 1165 1166 export default async function Page() { 1167 const data = await fetchData() 1168 return
{/* render data */}
1169 } 1170 ``` 1171 1172 > **Good to know**: Use the [taint API](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/taint) to prevent accidentally passing sensitive server values to Client Components. 1173 1174 For client-accessible values, use the `NEXT_PUBLIC_` prefix: 1175 1176 ```bash filename=".env.local" 1177 NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL="/api" 1178 ``` 1179 1180 ```tsx filename="app/components/client-component.tsx" 1181 'use client' 1182 1183 export default function ClientComponent() { 1184 const apiUrl = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL 1185 return

{config}

1198 } 1199 ``` 1200 1201 Learn more about [environment variables](/docs/app/guides/environment-variables). 1202 1203 ### `devIndicators` Options 1204 1205 The following options have been removed from [`devIndicators`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/devIndicators): 1206 1207 - `appIsrStatus` 1208 - `buildActivity` 1209 - `buildActivityPosition` 1210 1211 The indicator itself remains available. 1212 1213 ### `experimental.dynamicIO` and `experimental.useCache` 1214 1215 The `experimental.dynamicIO` and `experimental.useCache` flags are deprecated. This optimizes how Next.js prefetches and caches navigation data: 585 586 - **Layout deduplication**: When prefetching multiple URLs with a shared layout, the layout is downloaded once. 587 - **Incremental prefetching**: Next.js only prefetches parts not already in cache, rather than entire pages. 588 589 These changes require **no code modifications** and are designed to improve performance across all apps. 590 591 However, you may see more individual prefetch requests with much lower total transfer sizes. This reduces revalidation cost for images without cache-control headers. 725 726 For some Next.js users, image revalidation was happening frequently, often because the upstream source images missed a `cache-control` header. This caused revalidation to happen every `60` seconds, which increased CPU usage and cost. 727 728 Since most images do not change often, this short interval is not ideal. Setting the default to 4 hours offers a more durable cache by default, while still allowing images to update a few times per day if needed. 729 730 If you need the previous behavior, change `minimumCacheTTL` to a lower value, for example back to `60` seconds: 731 732 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 733 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 734 735 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 736 images: { 737 minimumCacheTTL: 60, 738 }, 739 } 740 741 export default nextConfig 742 ``` 743 744 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 745 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 746 const nextConfig = { 747 images: { 748 minimumCacheTTL: 60, 749 }, 750 } 751 752 module.exports = nextConfig 753 ``` 754 755 ### `imageSizes` Default (Breaking change) 756 757 The value `16` has been removed from the default `images.imageSizes` array. 758 759 We have looked at request analytics and found out that very few projects ever serve 16 pixels width images. Removing this setting reduces the size of the `srcset` attribute shipped to the browser by `next/image`. 760 761 If you need to support 16px images: 762 763 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 764 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 765 766 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 767 images: { 768 imageSizes: [16, 32, 48, 64, 96, 128, 256, 384], 769 }, 770 } 771 772 export default nextConfig 773 ``` 774 775 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 776 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 777 const nextConfig = { 778 images: { 779 imageSizes: [16, 32, 48, 64, 96, 128, 256, 384], 780 }, 781 } 782 783 module.exports = nextConfig 784 ``` 785 786 Rather than lack of developer usage, we believe 16 pixels width images have become less common, because `devicePixelRatio: 2` actually fetches a 32px image to prevent blurriness in retina displays. 787 788 ### `qualities` Default (Breaking change) 789 790 The default value for `images.qualities` has changed from allowing all qualities to only `[75]`. 791 792 If you need to support multiple quality levels: 793 794 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 795 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 796 797 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 798 images: { 799 qualities: [50, 75, 100], 800 }, 801 } 802 803 export default nextConfig 804 ``` 805 806 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 807 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 808 const nextConfig = { 809 images: { 810 qualities: [50, 75, 100], 811 }, 812 } 813 814 module.exports = nextConfig 815 ``` 816 817 If you specify a `quality` prop not included in the `image.qualities` array, the quality will be coerced to the closest value in `images.qualities`.     {posts.map((post) => (
  • {post.title}
    • ))}
) } ``` ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher export default async function Page() { let data = await fetch('https://api.vercel.app/blog') let posts = await data.json() return (
    {posts.map((post) => (
  • {post.title}
    • ))}
) } ``` ## `fetch(url, options)` Since Next.js extends the [Web `fetch()` API](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Fetch_API), you can use any of the [native options available](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/fetch#parameters). ### `options.cache` Configure how the request should interact with Next.js [caching](/docs/app/getting-started/caching). ```ts fetch(`https://...`, { cache: 'force-cache' | 'no-store' }) ``` - **`auto no cache`** (default): Next.js fetches the resource from the remote server on every request in development, but will fetch once during `next build` because the route will be statically prerendered. If [Request-time APIs](/docs/app/glossary#request-time-apis) are detected on the route, Next.js will fetch the resource on every request. - **`no-store`**: Next.js fetches the resource from the remote server on every request, even if Request-time APIs are not detected on the route. - **`force-cache`**: Next.js looks for a matching request in its server-side cache. - If there is a match and it is fresh, it will be returned from the cache. - If there is no match or a stale match, Next.js will fetch the resource from the remote server and update the cache with the downloaded resource. ### `options.next.revalidate` ```ts fetch(`https://...`, { next: { revalidate: false | 0 | number } }) ``` Set the cache lifetime of a resource (in seconds). - **`false`** - Cache the resource indefinitely. Semantically equivalent to `revalidate: Infinity`. The HTTP cache may evict older resources over time. - **`0`** - Prevent the resource from being cached. - **`number`** - (in seconds) Specify the resource should have a cache lifetime of at most `n` seconds. > **Good to know**: > > - If an individual `fetch()` request sets a `revalidate` number lower than the [default `revalidate`](/docs/app/guides/caching-without-cache-components#route-segment-config-revalidate) of a route, the whole route revalidation interval will be decreased. > - If two fetch requests with the same URL in the same route have different `revalidate` values, the lower value will be used. > - Conflicting options such as `{ revalidate: 3600, cache: 'no-store' }` are not allowed, both will be ignored, and in development mode a warning will be printed to the terminal. ### `options.next.tags` ```ts fetch(`https://...`, { next: { tags: ['collection'] } }) ``` Set the cache tags of a resource. Data can then be revalidated on-demand using [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag). The max length for a custom tag is 256 characters and the max tag items is 128. ## Memoization `fetch` requests using `GET` with the same URL and options are automatically [memoized](/docs/app/glossary#memoization) during a server render pass. If you call the same `fetch` in multiple Server Components, layouts, pages, `generateStaticParams` and `generateViewport`, Next.js executes it only once and shares the result. To opt out, pass an [`AbortController`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/AbortController) signal to `fetch`: ```js const { signal } = new AbortController() fetch(url, { signal }) ``` > **Good to know**: Memoization does not apply in [Route Handlers](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route), since they are not part of the React component tree. ## Troubleshooting ### Fetch default `auto no store` and `cache: 'no-store'` not showing fresh data in development Next.js caches `fetch` responses in Server Components across Hot Module Replacement (HMR) in local development for faster responses and to reduce costs for billed API calls. By default, the [HMR cache](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/serverComponentsHmrCache) applies to all fetch requests, including those with the default `auto no cache` and `cache: 'no-store'` option. This means uncached requests will not show fresh data between HMR refreshes. However, the cache will be cleared on navigation or full-page reloads. See the [`serverComponentsHmrCache`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/serverComponentsHmrCache) docs for more information. ### Hard refresh and caching in development In development mode, if the request includes the `cache-control: no-cache` header, `options.cache`, `options.next.revalidate`, and `options.next.tags` are ignored, and the `fetch` request is served from the source. Browsers typically include `cache-control: no-cache` when the cache is disabled in developer tools or during a hard refresh. ## Version History | Version | Changes | | --------- | ------------------- | | `v13.0.0` | `fetch` introduced. |

--- title: not-found.js description: API reference for the not-found.js file. --- Next.js provides two conventions to handle not found cases: - **`not-found.js`**: Used when you call the [`notFound`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/not-found) function in a route segment. - **`global-not-found.js`**: Used to define a global 404 page for unmatched routes across your entire app. This is handled at the routing level and doesn't depend on rendering a layout or page. ## `not-found.js` The **not-found** file is used to render UI when the [`notFound`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/not-found) function is thrown within a route segment. Along with serving a custom UI, Next.js will return a `200` HTTP status code for streamed responses, and `404` for non-streamed responses (see [Status Codes](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/loading#status-codes) for details about SEO). ```tsx filename="app/not-found.tsx" switcher import Link from 'next/link' export default function NotFound() { return (

Not Found

Could not find requested resource

Return Home
) } ``` ```jsx filename="app/blog/not-found.js" switcher import Link from 'next/link' export default function NotFound() { return (

Not Found

Could not find requested resource

Return Home
) } ``` In the [component hierarchy](/docs/app/getting-started/project-structure#component-hierarchy), `not-found.js` renders between `loading.js` and `page.js`. It is wrapped by the `` boundary from `loading.js` and the error boundary from `error.js` in the same segment. ## `global-not-found.js` (experimental) The `global-not-found.js` file lets you define a 404 page for your entire application. Unlike `not-found.js`, which works at the route level, this is used when a requested URL doesn't match any route at all. Next.js **skips rendering** and directly returns this global page. title: useRouter
description: API reference for the useRouter hook.
---

The `useRouter` hook allows you to programmatically change routes inside [Client Components](/docs/app/getting-started/server-and-client-components).

> **Recommendation:** Use the [`<Link>` component](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link) for navigation unless you have a specific requirement for using `useRouter`.

```tsx filename="app/example-client-component.tsx" switcher
'use client'

import { useRouter } from 'next/navigation'

export default function Page() {
  const router = useRouter()

  return (
    <button type="button" onClick={() => router.push('/dashboard')}>
      Dashboard
    </button>
  )
}
```

```jsx filename="app/example-client-component.js" switcher
'use client'

import { useRouter } from 'next/navigation'

export default function Page() {
  const router = useRouter()

  return (
    <button type="button" onClick={() => router.push('/dashboard')}>
      Dashboard
    </button>
  )
}
```

## `useRouter()`

- `router.push(href: string, { scroll: boolean, transitionTypes: string[] })`: Perform a client-side navigation to the provided route. Adds a new entry into the [browser's history stack](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/History_API). The optional `transitionTypes` are passed to [`React.addTransitionType`](https://react.dev/reference/react/addTransitionType) inside the navigation Transition.
- `router.replace(href: string, { scroll: boolean, transitionTypes: string[] })`: Perform a client-side navigation to the provided route without adding a new entry into the browser’s history stack. - **`404.js` → `app/not-found.tsx`**, **`_error.js` → `app/error.tsx` + `app/global-error.tsx`**. Note: in this Next.js version error boundaries receive **`unstable_retry`** instead of the older `reset` prop — the docs check caught that.
